islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Sources linger: a commitment law. The smell of a thing behind a wall is
# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world
# 7: eleven frames out of twelve on the same spot, the source hopping left and
# right of it). Here a painted source keeps ~94% of itself per thought after
# the paint moves on, so the wave still holds the place it was first told and
# the nearer of the two stays the target. Where the agent stands there is
# nothing: `here` and its ring erase the ghost (an eaten morsel leaves no
# ghost to circle).

channel source
channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

channel free

rule front:
  when 1

control.best:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1.189 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1.037
  set value = max(injection, max(0.8742 * max4(value), 0.8613 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

observations.text:
The agent walks south from the start, finds a patch of regrowing food around two brown rubble mounds west of centre, and spends roughly three quarters of its life circling those two mounds on the same loops, re-eating at the same four or five spots.
It is not stuck or pacing a wall — it eats — but it never leaves a region of about 15x15 cells while the map is full of food dots to the north, east and south that it never sees.
Only in the last quarter (the red track) does it break east through the doorway and eat once more on open ground, which shows the frontier pull exists but is drowned out by the smell of the known patch.
The void weighting cannot help here because the trouble is not the frontier marks but the nearby smell sources, which keep full weight however long the agent has been grazing there.
One mechanism: a slowly fading visit-density ("boredom") channel stamped where the agent walks, which discounts smell sources in heavily grazed ground so that after a few laps the frontier outweighs the local patch.

The agent spends the first third exploring well to the north-west and eats about nine times, then in the middle third (pink track) it circles round and round two small walled rooms just west of its start, a few cells across, which have food sitting inside them.
It never gets in: doors 0 and breaks 0, so it paces the outside of the room walls, pulled by the food it sees or smells inside, while the wave routes it round the room instead of into the wall.
Only late (red track) does it give up and walk south-east into open country, where it eats twice more; several other closed rooms with food dots inside are passed by the same way.
The failure is that a wall between the agent and visible food is treated as an obstacle to route around, not as something to press on.
One mechanism: make a solid cell that borders a room holding seen food or smell a source of its own (a door candidate), so the wave leads the agent straight into that wall where it presses INTERACT and opens the room.

turns.hypothesis: Confinement judged by the 8 neighbours sees a nook but not a dead-end region a few cells deep. A persistent ROOM channel — known free space blurred over the map, kept between thoughts — measures how open the region around each cell is, so sources and frontier marks inside pockets and corridors fade while those in open country (where more food and more frontier lie beyond) win. The agent commits to open regions and stops being pulled into dead pockets.

The agent remembers where it has walked: a TRAIL channel stamped under `here`, scrolling with the map and fading slowly. Cells on the trail pass on less of the wave and their sources count less, so stepping back onto the cell it just left is never the brightest choice — this breaks the two-cell limit cycle at a flipping smell bearing and pushes the agent onto fresh ground, while confinement suppression keeps nooks from dominating.

All frontier marks are equally faint, so the agent explores the nearest edge of the known map even when only a sliver of unknown lies behind it. A persistent VOID channel diffuses "unknown" (neither free nor solid) over the map, so each frontier mark is weighted by how much undiscovered country lies behind it; the agent heads for big unexplored regions, where unseen food is, instead of nibbling the borders of what it already knows. Confinement suppression is kept.

The wave crosses unknown cells as cheaply as walked ones, so a smelled source behind unexplored ground draws the agent straight across terrain that is often wall, and it wastes ticks bumping and re-routing. Here the wave pays an extra toll to cross cells that are neither known free nor known solid (distrust of the unseen), so routes run through known-free ground and the agent reaches food on paths that exist, while the frontier itself (a source on the unknown edge) still pulls through the void weighting of the best law.

One wave mixes two different wants — food it smells or sees, and unknown ground to explore — so a regrowing patch nearby always outshines the faint frontier and the agent grazes one loop for thousands of ticks (observer, world 7). Here they are two separate waves, FOOD and EXPLORE, and a slow GRAZE field (stamped where the agent walks, diffused, fading over hundreds of ticks) discounts the food wave only where the agent has already been grazing; after a few laps of a patch the explore wave wins and the agent leaves for unseen country, and returns once the boredom has faded and the patch has regrown.

The wave values every morsel alike, so a lone berry one step away beats a rich patch of five a few steps further, and the agent spends its walking on singletons. A persistent CLUSTER field diffuses food evidence (seen morsels and smell) over the map and remembers it for a while, so a source counts in proportion to how much food lies around it: the agent travels to dense patches where one trip buys several meals (far-but-rich over near-but-poor), while confinement still keeps nooks from dominating.

The Bellman discount makes the nearest frontier mark always win, so the agent explores by dithering into every small unseen pocket beside it — pockets its eyes would clear anyway — instead of striding out. A PROXIMITY field (a short wave from `here`, through non-solid cells) marks ground close to the agent, and frontier marks are discounted there while smell and seen food are not: near food is still taken at once, but exploration becomes long straight strides toward distant unknown, which uncovers more food per tick. Void weighting and confinement are kept.

Every seen morsel enters the wave at full strength whatever it looks like, although the food differs fourfold in worth (berry 12, fruit 22, mushroom 32) and the eye reports a brightness for each. Here a seen thing is weighted by its BRIGHTNESS (a quality cue, sharpened by a square so differences matter) and silenced where a refusal is remembered (`bad`, and its ring), so the agent walks past a dim berry to a bright fruit or mushroom and never returns to a poison it has burned on; frontier marks keep the void weighting and confinement of the best law.

When two goals pull about equally (a smell bearing flipping round a wall, two equidistant frontiers) the agent steps back and forth and loses ticks; my earlier trail law (#4) fought this by damping the whole wave on walked ground, which slowed planning everywhere. Here planning is untouched — the wave runs in its own channel — and only the READ-OUT is biased: a short-lived RECENT mark under the agent's last few cells makes the step back onto them look worse, so the agent keeps going unless the way back is clearly better (momentum, a commitment held for a few steps).

Food REGROWS where it grew, yet the wave forgets a place the moment the morsel is gone, so the agent either circles a patch blindly (observer, world 7) or abandons it for good. A trap-line forager: a LARDER channel remembers for a long time every cell where a morsel was seen, and a RIPE clock on each cell is reset where the agent walks and grows back slowly, so a remembered place calls again only after it has had time to regrow. This feeds a FOOD wave kept separate from the EXPLORE wave (the split that held up on holdout, #7: 16.0), so the agent explores new country while nothing is ripe and returns along a route of ripened spots when it is.

Doors are the cheapest way into new country — a closed room behind one is full of unseen food (mushrooms live in caves) — but the wave treats a door only as a partly passable wall and so routes round it to the nearest open frontier. Here a solid cell whose LEAK has been taught above the innate guess (the body learned that this hue gives) becomes a DOOR source itself, worth more the more unknown lies behind it, so the agent seeks out learned doors and opens them; stone that taught leak downward gets nothing. Void weighting and confinement are kept for the rest.

A deterministic wave over a symmetric map leaves the agent like Buridan's ass: two frontiers or two smells of equal worth pull it back and forth, and on the same map it always makes the same choice, so a bad route is repeated. Here every map cell carries a WHIM — a random preference, resampled only rarely so it stays attached to the place as the map scrolls — and frontier and smell sources are scaled by it: ties are broken by a lasting arbitrary preference (a commitment that costs nothing to compute), and different parts of the frontier get tried instead of always the geometrically nearest. Void weighting and confinement are kept.

The observer saw the agent circle small closed rooms with food inside for a third of its life (world 2, doors 0): the wave only seeps through a wall at the leak fraction, so going round always looks cheaper and the wall is never pressed. Here a LURE field spreads seen and smelled food a few cells through open ground, and a solid cell that the lure reaches becomes a BREACH source at the lure's strength, so the wave leads straight into the wall between the agent and the food and it presses INTERACT. Food (with breaches) and exploration (frontier weighted by unknown, plus learned doors) run as two separate waves — the split that held on holdout (#7).

Some frontier marks never go away — unknown cells inside sealed rooms or behind rock, seen from outside but unreachable — and they keep pulling the agent round the same walls (the circling of world 2). Here each cell keeps a STALE clock that runs while it stays a bare frontier mark (no smell, no thing) and resets the moment it stops being one, and a frontier mark loses weight as it goes stale: fresh edges of the map pull, old unreachable ones fade, so the agent stops orbiting what it cannot reach. Learned doors, void weighting and confinement (#13, best raw) are kept.

The two best-supported pieces never met: separate FOOD and EXPLORE waves (the only structure that held on holdout, #7) and learned DOORS as sources of new country (#13, best raw). Here they are joined, without #7's grazing boredom (which collapsed world 6), and the two wants are kept honest in different ways: the food wave is a SINK at remembered refusals (`bad` and its ring pass no food wave, so a poison patch cannot draw the agent back), while the explore wave carries doors and void-weighted frontier and ignores food altogether. Each wave has one clear job, so tuning has fewer cross-coupled constants to overfit.

One discount rate serves two horizons badly: food is worth chasing only when near (a far smell is often a lie round a wall), while unexplored country is worth a long walk. Here two waves with DIFFERENT horizons: a SHORT wave from smelled and seen food that dies within a few cells, and a LONG wave from the frontier and void that crosses the whole map almost undiminished, so near food is always taken, but beyond a few cells the agent commits to the long-range plan of where unknown country lies instead of bending toward every distant smell.
